rules.title: Credential exposure
rules.description: Never log, return, persist, or commit provider API keys, session tokens, passwords, CSRF secrets, or encrypted credential plaintext.
rules.check: Trace credential values and verify they remain server-side and secret-free at API/log/UI boundaries.

rules.title: Authentication boundary
rules.description: Protected API routes must authenticate from the server-controlled session boundary and must not trust browser-supplied identity or roles.
rules.check: Verify every protected route has explicit authentication and rejects missing or invalid sessions.

rules.title: Authorization isolation
rules.description: Project, repository, work-item, credential, and execution data must be scoped to the authenticated user and authorized project membership.
rules.check: Check for cross-user or cross-project access paths and client-controlled authorization.

rules.title: Provider secret handling
rules.description: GitHub/OpenAI credentials must be encrypted at rest, resolved server-side, and never sourced from browser localStorage or request-body secrets.
rules.check: Verify provider adapters receive credentials only from the server-side credential boundary.

rules.title: CSRF protection
rules.description: State-changing authenticated browser operations must enforce the repository's CSRF contract.
rules.check: Verify POST/PATCH/DELETE mutations reject missing, invalid, or mismatched CSRF material where required.

rules.title: Input validation
rules.description: External input must be validated with Zod or an equivalent typed validation boundary before use.
rules.check: Check route params, request bodies, query parameters, and webhook payloads.

rules.title: Parameterized database access
rules.description: Use Drizzle/parameterized queries; never concatenate untrusted values into SQL.
rules.check: Inspect all modified queries for injection risk and accidental broad reads.

rules.title: Migration correctness
rules.description: Schema changes require the repository's migration mechanism and must preserve production compatibility.
rules.check: Verify new tables/indexes/constraints exist in production migrations and handle existing data safely.

rules.title: Transaction and replacement semantics
rules.description: Multi-step persistence and credential replacement operations must be atomic and must not leave stale or duplicate rows.
rules.check: Look for race conditions, duplicate credential rows, partial writes, and rollback gaps.

rules.title: API contract correctness
rules.description: Responses must follow the documented {data,error,meta} shape and use the documented HTTP status semantics.
rules.check: Verify success/error payloads and status codes for changed endpoints.

rules.title: Error leakage
rules.description: Provider, database, and authentication failures must not expose stack traces, credentials, internal tokens, or implementation details.
rules.check: Inspect error translation and logging behavior.

rules.title: Server/client boundary
rules.description: Secrets, privileged provider calls, authorization, and database access must remain on the server and must not leak into Client Components.
rules.check: Check use of server APIs, client boundaries, environment variables, and browser bundles.

rules.title: GitHub integration trust boundary
rules.description: GitHub repository/tree/issue operations must validate repository ownership and credentials server-side and must safely handle truncated or hostile API data.
rules.check: Verify provider boundary, response validation, and untrusted GitHub data handling.

rules.title: Regression tests
rules.description: Security and bug fixes require deterministic behavioral tests that would fail on the old behavior.
rules.check: Verify changed security/API/database behavior has focused regression coverage.

rules.title: Test quality
rules.description: Tests should exercise public behavior, avoid tautological assertions, and cover negative authorization and validation paths.
rules.check: Look for missing failure cases and implementation-coupled tests.

rules.title: CI action pinning
rules.description: Third-party GitHub Actions used for security-sensitive CI should be pinned to reviewed commit SHAs rather than mutable tags.
rules.check: Check workflow action references and least-privilege permissions.
